hook: Graphs with no vertex in every triangle must have about as many triangles as their spectral radius
summary: The authors prove that such a graph has at least its adjacency spectral radius minus a constant in triangles, which is stronger than a conjecture of Li, Feng and Peng. They bound the sum of squared eigenvalues, use interlacing and perturbation estimates to pin down a vertex neighborhood, then count triangles with weights. The bound applies when the spectral radius exceeds the square root of the edge count.
title: Triangles without a common vertex
